title: Keep defence spending at about 5% of GDP and fund the armed forces' needs
description: The coalition agreement signed in June 2026 kept the ambition of defence spending of around 5% of GDP (according to coalition partner Virginijus Sinkevičius, leader of the Democrats 'For Lithuania'), and the government programme approved by the Seimas on 14 July 2026 promises defence funding that 'fully meets the needs and recommendations of the armed forces', with priority for air defence, protection against drones and the Baltic Defence Line.
reasoning: The draft 2027–2029 state budget approved by the government on 16 October 2026 allocates €4.8 billion to the Ministry of National Defence, State Defence Fund included, which the government puts at 5% of GDP (down from 5.38% in 2026 because GDP grows faster than the allocation). The budget still has to be adopted by the Seimas, and Sinkevičius acknowledged in October that only about half of the 2026 defence budget had been spent by early autumn, so the verdict depends on adoption and execution.
key_evidence: LRT, 14 July 2026: the programme promises defence funding that fully meets the needs and recommendations of the armed forces
LRT/ELTA, 22 October 2026: Virginijus Sinkevičius says the coalition keeps 'the 5% ambition'
Government, 16 October 2026: Ministry of National Defence and State Defence Fund €4.8 billion in 2027, i.e. 5% of GDP (5.38% in 2026)
LRT, 22 October 2026: the Prime Minister says he is not satisfied with the pace of defence spending and has the defence minister's assurance the money will be used

title: Urgently deploy an air-threat detection and counter-drone defence system
description: After repeated drone and balloon incursions from Belarus, the July 2026 programme pledges to 'urgently put into operation an air threat detection and defence system, particularly for protection against unmanned aerial vehicles, and further develop public warning systems' (as quoted by LRT).
reasoning: The government reports that a pilot Ukrainian-developed 'SkyFortress' system is being deployed, acoustic sensors installed on the border and air-surveillance capacity reinforced with mobile radars, and that legal changes giving border guards clearer powers against hybrid threats have been initiated. After a drone carrying explosives fell in Pasvalys district on 18 October 2026, the National Security Commission met to consider additional powers to neutralise drones. The system is not yet complete, and opposition leader Laurynas Kasčiūnas says the 2027 budget promises 'no breakthrough' in air defence.
key_evidence: LRT English newsletter, July 2026: programme quotation on the air-threat detection and counter-UAV system
Government 100-day report, 21 October 2026: SkyFortress pilot, acoustic sensors, mobile radars, planned powers for border guards
LRT, 19 October 2026: National Security Commission meeting after a drone entered from Poland and exploded in Pasvalys district; extra powers to neutralise drones on the agenda
LRT, 20 October 2026: Kasčiūnas (TS-LKD) says there will be no breakthrough in air defence

title: Raise old-age pensions by about 10% in 2027
description: The programme makes higher pensions and less poverty among older people a priority. On 2 October 2026 Sinkevičius said his aim was a 10% rise in old-age pensions in 2027 (about €75–76 on average), using part of the surplus of the Sodra social-insurance reserve on top of statutory indexation (about 8.5%).
reasoning: The draft 2027 budget approved by the government on 16 October 2026 provides an extra €715.5 million for old-age pensions, raising the average old-age pension by 10.4% (€78, from €747 to €825) and by 10.9% (€88, to €895) for people with the required insurance record, for 659,000 pensioners. The increase takes effect only if the Seimas adopts the state and Sodra budgets this autumn.
key_evidence: LRT/BNS, 2 October 2026: Sinkevičius aims at a 10% rise, partly financed from the Sodra reserve surplus
LRT, 14 July 2026: programme priorities include raising pensions and reducing poverty among older people
Government, 16 October 2026: +10.4% average old-age pension (€747 to €825), +10.9% with the required record; €715.5 million

title: Ensure parents' income does not fall after a child is born (higher childcare benefits)
description: Making sure that 'the income of families and parents who have had children does not fall' was presented by Sinkevičius to the Seimas in June 2026 as a coalition priority. The family package of the Ministry of Social Security and Labour proposes raising the childcare benefit (for the 18-month leave option) to 100% of the average net wage.
reasoning: The ministry planned to raise the benefits from 1 January 2028, and the draft 2027 budget submitted in October 2026 contains no money for it, which coalition partners criticised. On 22 October Sinkevičius said the coalition was seeking consensus to raise the benefits from 1 July 2027; the deputy minister said this would need just over €60 million that is not yet in the Sodra budget. The other family-package measures (€150 million) are in the draft.
key_evidence: LRT, 29 June 2026: Sinkevičius tells the Seimas the programme provides that parents' income will not fall after a birth
LRT, 22 October 2026: the ministry planned the increase from 2028; no funds in the draft 2027 budget
LRT, 22 October 2026: the Prime Minister says the coalition agreed to aim for 1 July 2027
Government, 16 October 2026: family package of €150 million in the draft (childcare and employment guarantees, housing support, pension guarantees, first-grader allowance)

title: Expand support for families buying their first home
description: Additional support for first-time home buyers is one of the cost-of-living and demographic measures of the programme presented by Sinkevičius in July 2026.
reasoning: The draft 2027 budget earmarks €40 million for support to buy a home, adding funding to the existing scheme and extra incentives in the regions. The measure depends on the Seimas adopting the budget, and no change in the number of beneficiaries can yet be measured.
key_evidence: LRT, 7 July 2026: the programme includes expanded support for first-time homebuyers
Government, 16 October 2026: €40 million for housing purchase support in the 2027 draft budget

title: Free meals for primary-school pupils in all schools
description: According to LRT, the programme plans free meals for primary school pupils in all schools, alongside more funding for non-formal education.
reasoning: The government's 100-day report of 21 October 2026 says its family package provides for gradually extending free meals to pupils in grades 5–10, but the itemised family-package allocations of the draft 2027 budget (childcare and employment guarantees, housing support, pension guarantees, the first-grader allowance) do not mention school meals, and no adopted decision was found. The evidence is thin, hence the low confidence.
key_evidence: LRT, 14 July 2026: free meals for primary school students in all schools among the programme's plans
Government 100-day report, 21 October 2026: gradual extension of free meals to grades 5–10 announced
Government, 16 October 2026: the itemised 2027 family-package allocations do not include school meals

title: Temporarily halt increases in the excise duty on diesel
description: For businesses, the programme approved on 14 July 2026 promises to temporarily halt increases in the diesel fuel excise duty (LRT).
reasoning: Under the Excise Law the CO2 component of the diesel excise is due to rise by 7.74 cents to 13.1 cents per litre in 2027, and the draft 2027 budget includes that increase. On 22 October 2026 Sinkevičius said the government would propose raising fuel excise by less than planned, with a decision probably in an extraordinary Seimas session in early 2027, because the scheduled rises are tied to commitments under the EU Recovery and Resilience Facility. What is now proposed is a smaller rise, not a halt; no decision has been taken yet.
key_evidence: LRT, 14 July 2026: programme promise to temporarily halt diesel excise increases
LRT/BNS, 22 October 2026: the 2027 CO2 component for diesel is scheduled at 13.1 cents per litre (+7.74 cents); the draft budget includes it
LRT/BNS, 22 October 2026: the Prime Minister says the increase will be smaller than planned, decided probably in early 2027

title: Introduce progressive taxation for the highest earners
description: The programme approved on 14 July 2026 plans to introduce progressive taxation for the highest earners and to review public-sector salary rules (LRT).
reasoning: No bill raising taxes on top earners accompanied the draft 2027–2029 budget, whose additional revenue is to come mainly from tax-administration measures (€197 million) and spending cuts of about €90 million. In October 2026 Liberal leader Viktorija Čmilytė-Nielsen said Finance Minister Taurimas Valys had hinted that the Social Democrats had a new tax package 'in the drawer' that could not yet be discussed publicly. No concrete step had been taken as of October 2026.
key_evidence: LRT, 14 July 2026: progressive taxation for the highest earners among the programme's plans
Government, 16 October 2026: the draft 2027 budget relies on €197 million from better tax administration and 0.5% cuts in ministries' appropriations
LRT, 22 October 2026: Čmilytė-Nielsen says the finance minister hinted at an unpublished tax package

title: Cushion rising prices by raising incomes faster than prices
description: Sinkevičius told the Seimas in July 2026 that rising prices would be among his government's biggest challenges; the programme pledges to reduce their impact by increasing incomes more quickly, strengthening price monitoring and fair competition, and reducing income inequality.
reasoning: The draft 2027 budget proposes raising the minimum monthly wage by 8%, from €1,153 to €1,245, and allocates €450.2 million to pay rises, including 7.56% for teachers, researchers and coaches and 7.5% for culture workers and statutory officers, which the finance minister says will lift incomes faster than inflation. In response to fuel prices the government also cut regional train fares by 50% from October to the end of 2026 and announced the same discount for intercity buses. The budget is not yet adopted and the effect on purchasing power cannot yet be measured.
key_evidence: LRT, 14 July 2026: programme pledge to reduce the impact of rising prices by increasing incomes more quickly
Government, 16 October 2026: minimum wage +8% to €1,245; €450.2 million for public-sector pay
Government 100-day report, 21 October 2026: 50% discount on regional train tickets from October to year-end; intercity buses to follow

title: Normalise diplomatic relations with China
description: The programme aims to normalise diplomatic relations with China, downgraded since 2021 after Vilnius allowed a 'Taiwanese Representative Office' to open, to the level of representation other EU states have.
reasoning: On 14 October 2026 Sinkevičius said the government had adopted an action plan with concrete steps and deadlines to restore diplomatic representation, handled by Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys, and that he expected clear progress by the end of the year, while noting that the outcome is not only in Lithuania's hands. As of then representation had not been restored; according to BNS no Chinese diplomat has been in Lithuania since May 2025.
key_evidence: LRT, 14 July 2026: the programme aims to normalise diplomatic relations with China
LRT/BNS, 14 October 2026: action plan with steps and deadlines; progress expected by year-end
China downgraded relations to chargé d'affaires level in 2021; no Chinese diplomats in Lithuania since May 2025 (BNS)

title: Continue support for Ukraine against Russia's aggression
description: The programme pledges continued support for Ukraine in its fight against Russia's aggression and keeping pressure, including sanctions, on Russia.
reasoning: The commitment is open-ended and has been maintained so far. On 13 October 2026 Sinkevičius discussed military-technical and humanitarian aid, including air-defence means, with President Volodymyr Zelensky and promised that Lithuania's 2027 EU Council presidency would rally support for Ukraine's accession; the government says that at Lithuania's initiative EU individual sanctions on Russia were extended for three years and that it is seeking an EU ban on the transit of Russian food grain.
key_evidence: LRT, 14 July 2026: programme pledge of continued support for Ukraine
Government, 13 October 2026: phone call with Zelensky on military-technical, humanitarian and air-defence aid
Government 100-day report: EU individual sanctions on Russia extended for three years; tighter checks on grain transit from Russia and Belarus

title: Seek full membership of CERN
description: Full membership of the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN), of which Lithuania has been an associate member since 2018, is a goal written into the 21st government's programme.
reasoning: In August 2026 Sinkevičius sent CERN's leadership an official letter applying for full membership, and in October he discussed it with the president of the CERN Council. Membership requires a decision by CERN's member states, so the pledge is under way but not yet fulfilled.
key_evidence: Government, 26 August 2026: official letter to CERN on full membership; the goal is in the government programme
Government, 20 October 2026: meeting with the CERN Council president
